intended_object: The canonical projection from a product ∏ᵢ Aᵢ of topological monoids onto the i-th factor, as a continuous monoid homomorphism, i.e. evaluation at i. The docstring says so and calls it the indexed-product analogue of `ContinuousMonoidHom.fst`/`snd`.
explanation:
The body pairs `Pi.evalMonoidHom A i`, which is the monoid homomorphism f ↦ f i, with `continuous_apply i`, which says evaluation at i is continuous for the product topology. That is exactly the i-th projection, viewed as a continuous monoid homomorphism.

The generality is the natural one. The index type ι is arbitrary, and the factors only need to be monoids with a topology; continuous multiplication is not required. Monoids are what the `→ₜ*` structure needs anyway.

This Mathlib version has no matching declaration. `Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom.lean` defines `fst`, `snd`, `inl`, `inr` and similar maps for binary products, but no indexed-product projection. I also grepped Mathlib for `→ₜ*` maps out of `∀ i, A i` and found none.

The additive version produced by `to_additive` is likewise correct.
